questions.question: Which living ingredient makes bread dough rise?
questions.note: Yeast feeds on sugars and releases carbon dioxide, which inflates the dough.

questions.question: What plant makes up most of a giant panda’s diet?
questions.note: Wild giant pandas spend much of the day eating bamboo.

questions.question: In tennis scoring, what does “love” mean?
questions.note: Love is the standard tennis term for a score of zero.

questions.question: Which river flows beneath London’s Tower Bridge?
questions.note: Tower Bridge crosses the River Thames in central London.

questions.question: Who sings lead on the Beatles’ 1966 single “Yellow Submarine”?
questions.note: Ringo Starr sings the lead vocal; the other Beatles join the choruses.

questions.question: After breathing normal air, we exhale mostly which gas?
questions.note: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of inhaled air and remains the largest part of exhaled air.

questions.question: What is allspice made from?
questions.note: Allspice is the dried, unripe berry of the Pimenta dioica tree.

questions.question: Penguins expel their salt glands’ secretions through what?
questions.note: Their salt glands drain into the nasal passages, so excess salt leaves through the nostrils.

questions.question: In Carroll’s Alice in Wonderland, the Duchess’s baby turns into what?
questions.note: Alice carries the baby away before it transforms into a pig.

questions.question: Ming, the animal dated to 507 years old, was what?
questions.note: Ming was an ocean quahog clam collected near Iceland.

questions.question: Margarine’s original French recipe got its main fat from what?
questions.note: Hippolyte Mège-Mouriès made early margarine largely from beef fat.

questions.question: At Heinz’s 1869 launch, what was its first bottled product?
questions.note: Henry Heinz first sold his mother’s grated horseradish in clear bottles.

questions.question: What color are Dorothy’s magic slippers in the 1939 Wizard of Oz?
questions.note: The film changed the book’s silver shoes to ruby slippers to exploit Technicolor.

questions.question: A leaf from which tree appears on Canada’s national flag?
questions.note: The flag centers a stylized red maple leaf.

questions.question: The fuzzy side of a Velcro fastener is covered in tiny what?
questions.note: One strip has hooks; the softer strip has loops for those hooks to catch.

questions.question: Which part of your eye changes the size of your pupil?
questions.note: Muscles in the iris constrict or dilate the pupil to control incoming light.

questions.question: The Taj Mahal’s main white marble building was built as what?
questions.note: Shah Jahan commissioned the complex as a mausoleum for Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.question: What bird’s head forms the handle of Mary Poppins’ umbrella?
questions.note: Mary Poppins carries an umbrella with a talking parrot-head handle.

questions.question: In 1971’s Willy Wonka, the machine that rejects Veruca tests what?
questions.note: The Eggdicator judges golden chocolate eggs as good or bad.

questions.question: In classic Clue, what must you still try to do after a wrong accusation?
questions.note: You stop moving and suggesting, but must still show cards to disprove others’ suggestions.

questions.question: What does a tape measure’s sliding end hook compensate for?
questions.note: The hook slides by its own thickness so inside and outside measurements agree.

questions.question: What gives ordinary aluminum foil its shiny and dull sides?
questions.note: Two sheets are rolled together at the final pass. The sides touching the rollers become shiny.

questions.question: Which kitchen tool did Jackson Pollock use to squeeze paint onto canvas?
questions.note: Pollock used hardened brushes, sticks, and even a kitchen baster to drip and pour paint.

questions.question: In soccer, a legal throw-in goes directly into your own goal. What next?
questions.note: A goal cannot be scored directly from a throw-in. Into your own goal means a corner kick.

questions.question: What was the fake blood in the shower scene of Psycho made from?
questions.note: The black-and-white film used chocolate syrup because its tone and flow read well on camera.

questions.question: Which candy did E.T. follow in E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial?
questions.note: Elliott lays a trail of Reese’s Pieces to coax E.T. out of hiding.

questions.question: What make of car is the time machine in Back to the Future?
questions.note: Doc Brown builds the time machine from a stainless-steel DeLorean DMC-12.

questions.question: David Bowie was born with which surname?
questions.note: He was born David Robert Jones and changed his stage name to avoid confusion with Davy Jones.

questions.question: What was the working title of the Beatles song “Yesterday”?
questions.note: McCartney used “Scrambled Eggs” as a placeholder while developing the melody.

questions.question: The name ABBA is formed from what?
questions.note: ABBA takes one initial from Agnetha, Björn, Benny, and Anni-Frid.

questions.question: Which actor provided Darth Vader’s speaking voice in the original Star Wars trilogy?
questions.note: David Prowse played Vader physically, while James Earl Jones supplied the voice.

questions.question: Toy Story was the first feature film made entirely with what?
questions.note: Pixar’s 1995 release was the first fully computer-animated feature film.

questions.question: In golf, what does a birdie mean?
questions.note: A birdie is a score of one stroke under par on a hole.

questions.question: How many feathers are traditionally used in a badminton shuttlecock?
questions.note: Competition feather shuttlecocks use 16 feathers fixed into the cork base.

questions.question: What color jersey marks the overall leader of the Tour de France?
questions.note: The race leader wears the yellow jersey, or maillot jaune.

questions.question: How many balls make up a standard over in modern cricket?
questions.note: An over consists of six valid deliveries by one bowler.

questions.question: Why does a volleyball libero wear a contrasting jersey?
questions.note: The different jersey lets officials track the libero’s special substitution and position rules.

questions.question: How many points is the black ball worth in snooker?
questions.note: The black is the highest-value color ball at seven points.

questions.question: The modern marathon distance is 26 miles plus how many yards?
questions.note: The official distance is 26 miles 385 yards, or 42.195 kilometers.

questions.question: What is Wimbledon’s playing surface?
questions.note: Wimbledon is the only tennis Grand Slam still played on grass.

questions.question: Botanically, peanuts belong to which family?
questions.note: Peanuts grow in pods and belong to the legume family with peas and beans.

questions.question: Capers are usually pickled parts of a plant. Which parts?
questions.note: Capers are unopened flower buds from the caper bush.

questions.question: Which spice is the dried stigma of a flower?
questions.note: Saffron consists of hand-picked stigmas from the saffron crocus.

questions.question: Nutmeg and mace come from what relationship?
options: One tree’s seed and seed covering
questions.note: Nutmeg is the seed; mace is the lacy red covering around that seed.

questions.question: Traditional Worcestershire sauce contains which fish?
questions.note: Anchovies ferment with vinegar, molasses, tamarind, and seasonings in the classic sauce.

questions.question: What does the Italian name tiramisu roughly mean?
questions.note: The name comes from an Italian phrase meaning “pick me up” or “cheer me up.”

questions.question: The modern chocolate chip cookie was created at which inn?
questions.note: Ruth Wakefield developed the cookie at Massachusetts’s Toll House Inn.

questions.question: Before small table forks caught on in Europe, forks were mainly used for what?
questions.note: Ancient forks were largely cooking tools; small personal eating forks spread much later.

questions.question: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.note: Two hearts pump blood to the gills and one pumps it around the body.

questions.question: What unusual shape are wombat droppings?
questions.note: Wombats produce cube-shaped droppings due to the changing elasticity of their intestines.

questions.question: What color is a polar bear’s skin under its fur?
questions.note: Polar bears have black skin beneath translucent, light-scattering fur.

questions.question: A giraffe has how many neck vertebrae?
questions.note: Like most mammals, a giraffe has seven neck vertebrae, each one greatly elongated.

questions.question: Flamingos get their pink color mainly from what?
questions.note: Carotenoid pigments from algae and small crustaceans color their feathers.

questions.question: Which planet has a day longer than its year?
questions.note: Venus rotates once in about 243 Earth days but orbits the Sun in about 225.

questions.question: What color can sunsets appear on Mars?
questions.note: Fine Martian dust scatters light so the sky near the setting Sun can look blue.

questions.question: Which planet is hottest, despite not being closest to the Sun?
questions.note: Venus’s thick carbon-dioxide atmosphere traps enough heat to make it hotter than Mercury.

questions.question: What does the “WD” in WD-40 stand for?
questions.note: The product name records “Water Displacement” and the successful 40th formula.

questions.question: Pencil “lead” is actually made mainly from what?
questions.note: Pencil cores use graphite mixed with clay, not metallic lead.

questions.question: Bubble Wrap was first marketed as what?
questions.note: Its inventors first tried selling the sealed-air plastic sheets as textured wallpaper.

questions.question: What does ZIP in ZIP Code stand for?
questions.note: The U.S. Postal Service introduced the Zone Improvement Plan code in 1963.

questions.question: Big Ben is properly the nickname of what?
questions.note: Big Ben names the Great Bell; the tower itself is Elizabeth Tower.

questions.question: Which country lies in all four hemispheres?
questions.note: Kiribati crosses both the equator and the 180-degree meridian.

questions.question: What is the world’s deepest lake?
questions.note: Siberia’s Lake Baikal reaches about 1,620 meters at its deepest point.

questions.question: The Statue of Liberty’s outer skin is made from what metal?
questions.note: Thin copper sheets form the exterior; oxidation created the green patina.

questions.question: What was the first music video shown on MTV?
questions.note: MTV launched on August 1, 1981, with the Buggles video Video Killed the Radio Star.

questions.question: The film sound-effect technique called Foley is named after a person with what first name?
questions.note: Sound-effects artist Jack Foley pioneered the synchronized performance technique that bears his name.

questions.question: How tall is an Oscar statuette?
questions.note: The Academy Award statuette stands 13.5 inches tall and weighs 8.5 pounds.

questions.question: Which film first used the famous Wilhelm scream sound effect?
questions.note: The scream was originally recorded for the 1951 film Distant Drums before later receiving its nickname.

questions.question: What song does Sam repeatedly play in Casablanca?
questions.note: Sam plays Herman Hupfeld's As Time Goes By for Ilsa and later for Rick.

questions.question: Which 1983 film was the first theatrical release to use the THX sound system?
questions.note: THX debuted with Return of the Jedi at the film's 1983 premiere.

questions.question: What nickname did the crew give the mechanical shark in Jaws?
questions.note: The Jaws crew called its troublesome mechanical shark Bruce.

questions.question: Which Disney animated feature was the first released in CinemaScope?
questions.note: Lady and the Tramp became Disney's first animated feature produced in the widescreen CinemaScope format.

questions.question: How far is a soccer penalty mark from the goal line?
questions.note: The penalty mark sits 12 yards from the midpoint between the goalposts.

questions.question: How many double stitches are on a regulation Major League baseball?
questions.note: A regulation baseball has 108 double stitches sewn into its cover.

questions.question: How high is the top edge of a regulation basketball rim?
questions.note: Basketball rules place the rim 10 feet above the playing floor.

questions.question: What is the official height of a table-tennis net?
questions.note: The net assembly must be 15.25 centimeters high along its entire length.

questions.question: How many sides does baseball's home plate have?
questions.note: Home plate is a five-sided slab with a 17-inch edge facing the pitcher.

questions.question: How long may a golfer search for a lost ball under the current rules?
questions.note: A ball is lost if it is not found within three minutes after the search begins.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of clubs a golfer may carry during a round?
questions.note: The Rules of Golf limit a player to 14 clubs during a round.

questions.question: A pineapple develops from roughly what structure?
questions.note: A pineapple is a multiple fruit formed as many individual flowers fuse together.

questions.question: Vanilla beans are the fruits of what kind of plant?
questions.note: Commercial vanilla comes from the cured fruits of climbing orchids in the genus Vanilla.

questions.question: Where does a cashew nut grow on its fruit?
questions.note: The cashew seed hangs in a shell from the bottom of the fleshy cashew apple.

questions.question: Cream of tartar is a crystalline by-product of making what?
questions.note: Cream of tartar is purified potassium bitartrate deposited during wine fermentation and aging.

questions.question: What physical test is traditionally used to sort ripe cranberries?
questions.note: Sound cranberries bounce, allowing damaged berries to be separated by bounce-board sorters.

questions.question: What gives tonic water its characteristic bitterness?
questions.note: Tonic water is flavored with the bitter alkaloid quinine.

questions.question: Which fruit supplies the enzyme bromelain used as a meat tenderizer?
questions.note: Pineapple tissues contain bromelain, a mixture of protein-digesting enzymes.

questions.question: An owl's eyes are shaped more like what than balls?
questions.note: An owl has elongated, tube-shaped eyes held rigidly in bony structures called sclerotic rings.

questions.question: Which marine mammal has the densest fur?
questions.note: Sea otters can have up to about one million hairs per square inch of fur.

questions.question: Butterflies primarily taste with receptors located where?
questions.note: Taste receptors on a butterfly's feet help it identify suitable food and host plants.

questions.question: What color can reindeer eyes turn during the Arctic winter?
questions.note: Reindeer tapeta change from gold in summer to deep blue in winter to improve low-light sensitivity.

questions.question: How often does a typical three-toed sloth descend from its tree to defecate?
questions.note: Three-toed sloths usually make a risky descent to the forest floor about once a week.

questions.question: Which bird has nostrils located near the tip of its bill?
questions.note: Unlike most birds, kiwis have nostrils near the tip of their long bills.

questions.question: What is the only venomous primate known to science?
questions.note: Slow lorises produce venom from a gland on the upper arm and deliver it through a bite.

questions.question: At sea-level pressure, how hot can a lightning channel become?
questions.note: A lightning channel can heat surrounding air to roughly 30,000 degrees Celsius.

questions.question: Which element was detected in the Sun before it was found on Earth?
questions.note: Helium was identified in the Sun's spectrum in 1868 before terrestrial helium was isolated.

questions.question: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
questions.note: The stirrup-shaped stapes in the middle ear is the body's smallest bone.

questions.question: What is absolute zero on the Celsius scale?
questions.note: Absolute zero is exactly 0 kelvin, equivalent to -273.15 degrees Celsius.

questions.question: What is the temperature of water's triple point?
questions.note: Pure water's solid, liquid, and vapor phases coexist at 0.01 degrees Celsius at the triple point.

questions.question: Why can no ordinary sound be heard in a vacuum?
options: Sound needs matter to carry vibrations
questions.note: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs particles in a medium to transmit its vibrations.

questions.question: Roughly how much DNA do humans and chimpanzees share?
questions.note: Comparisons of directly alignable DNA sequences put human-chimpanzee similarity at about 98.8 percent.

questions.question: Which country has the world's only national flag not shaped as a quadrilateral?
questions.note: Nepal's flag consists of two joined triangular pennants rather than a four-sided field.

questions.question: Which sea has no land coastline?
questions.note: The Sargasso Sea is bounded by rotating Atlantic currents rather than by land.

questions.question: Which country has three official capital cities?
questions.note: South Africa divides its executive, legislative, and judicial seats among Pretoria, Cape Town, and Bloemfontein.

questions.question: What is Bolivia's constitutional capital?
questions.note: Sucre is Bolivia's constitutional capital, while La Paz is the seat of government.

questions.question: Which sovereign country is entirely above 1,000 meters in elevation?
questions.note: Every part of Lesotho lies above 1,000 meters, giving it the world's highest lowest point.

questions.question: Which European country shares its longest land border with Brazil?
questions.note: French Guiana makes France's border with Brazil longer than any of France's European borders.

questions.question: Ecuador takes its name from which geographic feature?
questions.note: The country's Spanish name means equator, the line that crosses its territory.

questions.question: How many letter tiles are in an English-language Scrabble set?
questions.note: The standard English Scrabble distribution contains 100 tiles, including two blanks.

questions.question: How many possible arrangements does a standard 3-by-3 Rubik's Cube have?
questions.note: A standard Rubik's Cube has 43,252,003,274,489,856,000 possible configurations.

questions.question: Green Eggs and Ham was written using how many different words?
questions.note: Dr. Seuss wrote Green Eggs and Ham with a vocabulary of only 50 different words.

questions.question: Who illustrated the original published edition of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland?
questions.note: John Tenniel supplied the 42 illustrations for the 1865 published edition.

questions.question: In standard Monopoly, what happens when a player rolls doubles three times in one turn?
questions.note: Three consecutive doubles in one turn send the player immediately to Jail.

questions.question: Which chess piece may jump over other pieces?
questions.note: The knight is the only standard chess piece whose move can pass over intervening pieces.

questions.question: What shape is the original Pac-Man character based on?
questions.note: Creator Toru Iwatani said the character's shape was inspired by a pizza with one slice removed.

questions.question: Why do many ballpoint pen caps have a hole through the top?
questions.note: The hole allows some airflow if the cap is accidentally swallowed and blocks the airway.

questions.question: What was the tiny fifth pocket on blue jeans originally designed to hold?
questions.note: Levi Strauss describes the small pocket as a watch pocket made for pocket watches.

questions.question: What was the first product scanned with a UPC barcode in a store?
questions.note: A pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit gum became the first retail item scanned by UPC in 1974.

questions.question: Post-it Notes resulted from an attempt to invent what?
questions.note: 3M scientist Spencer Silver was trying to make a strong adhesive when he created a weak reusable one.

questions.question: The raised bumps on the F and J keyboard keys identify what?
questions.note: The tactile marks let touch typists locate the home-row index-finger keys without looking.

questions.question: What prevents microwaves from escaping through an oven door's viewing window?
questions.note: The perforated metal screen blocks microwave wavelengths while its smaller holes pass visible light.

questions.question: What kind of machine was the QWERTY keyboard layout developed for?
questions.note: Christopher Latham Sholes developed QWERTY for his early practical typewriter.

questions.question: The Bayeux Tapestry is technically what kind of textile?
questions.note: Its scenes are stitched in wool thread onto linen, making it an embroidery rather than a true tapestry.

questions.question: George Washington's dentures were never made from which commonly claimed material?
questions.note: Washington's dentures used materials including ivory, metal, and human or animal teeth, but not wood.

questions.question: Ancient Tyrian purple dye came mainly from what animals?
questions.note: Mediterranean craftspeople extracted Tyrian purple from secretions of predatory murex sea snails.

questions.question: What covered the Great Pyramid's rough core when it was new?
questions.note: Smooth white Tura limestone casing blocks originally covered the pyramid's core masonry.

questions.question: Where is the sling on Michelangelo's David?
options: Across his back and left hand
questions.note: David holds the sling over his left shoulder and down through his left hand.

questions.question: How tall was Napoleon Bonaparte according to a French medical measurement at his death?
questions.note: Converting the old French measurement puts Napoleon near 5 feet 6 inches in modern British units.

questions.question: The Liberty Bell's visible crack grew beyond repair during what event?
questions.note: The bell's final major crack widened while it rang for Washington's birthday in 1846.

decks.name: Set 3
decks.subtitle: Familiar territory, hidden details: 64 fresh facts across culture, play, nature, and daily life.

questions.question: What is the figure on an Academy Award statuette holding?
questions.note: The statuette depicts a knight holding a crusader sword while standing on a film reel.

questions.question: At the 1939 Academy Awards, how was Walt Disney honored for Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs?
options: With one full-size and seven miniature statuettes
questions.note: Shirley Temple presented Disney with one standard Oscar accompanied by seven miniature statuettes.

questions.question: Which member of Queen wrote "Another One Bites the Dust"?
questions.note: Queen bassist John Deacon wrote the song and its famous bass line.

questions.question: The THX cinema sound heard before films is officially called what?
questions.note: THX calls its swelling audio trademark the Deep Note.

questions.question: Which instrument plays the opening solo in George Gershwin's "Rhapsody in Blue"?
questions.note: The work opens with a clarinet trill that climbs into a long glissando.

questions.question: What was Mickey Mouse's first spoken phrase in a cartoon?
questions.note: Mickey first spoke in The Karnival Kid, where his first words were "Hot dogs!"

questions.question: Which singer wrote the Dolly Parton hit "I Will Always Love You"?
questions.note: Dolly Parton wrote and first recorded the song years before Whitney Houston's version.

questions.question: On Sesame Street, what is the Count's full title and name?
questions.note: The number-loving vampire Muppet is formally named Count von Count.

questions.question: Which film introduced the song "When You Wish Upon a Star"?
questions.note: Jiminy Cricket sings the song at the beginning of Disney's Pinocchio.

questions.question: How many strikes are rolled in a perfect ten-pin bowling game?
questions.note: A 300 game needs strikes in all ten frames plus two bonus deliveries in the tenth.

questions.question: May a chess king legally move onto a square attacked by an opponent?
questions.note: A king may not move onto an attacked square because that would leave it in check.

questions.question: How many points is a try worth in rugby union before any conversion?
questions.note: World Rugby awards five points for grounding the ball for a try.

questions.question: In baseball, a fly ball that strikes a foul pole is ruled what?
questions.note: The foul poles stand in fair territory, so a fair fly striking one above the fence is a home run.

questions.question: In boxing, where must the standing boxer wait during a knockdown count?
questions.note: The boxer who scored the knockdown must go to the farthest neutral corner during the count.

questions.question: In table tennis, what happens when an otherwise legal serve clips the net and lands correctly?
questions.note: That serve is a let, so no point is scored and the service is taken again.

questions.question: After a touchdown in American football, how far is a successful kick worth?
questions.note: The kick try after a touchdown scores one additional point.

questions.question: In Formula 1, what does a black flag with an orange circle tell a driver?
options: The car has a mechanical problem
questions.note: The black-and-orange flag warns that a car has a mechanical problem likely to endanger others.

questions.question: In basketball, how many personal fouls disqualify an NBA player?
questions.note: An NBA player is disqualified after committing a sixth personal foul.

questions.question: Which part of a cinnamon tree becomes the familiar spice?
questions.note: Cinnamon is prepared from the dried inner bark of trees in the genus Cinnamomum.

questions.question: What gas traditionally creates the holes in Swiss cheese?
questions.note: Bacteria release carbon dioxide during ripening, forming the holes known as eyes.

questions.question: Aquafaba, used as an egg-white substitute, is usually the cooking liquid from what?
questions.note: Aquafaba is the protein- and starch-containing liquid left from cooking chickpeas or found in a can of them.

questions.question: Cloves are dried parts of a tree. Which parts?
questions.note: Cloves are the dried unopened flower buds of the clove tree.

questions.question: Which cocoa component is absent from standard white chocolate?
questions.note: White chocolate uses cocoa butter but contains no nonfat cocoa solids.

questions.question: Brazil nuts develop inside what kind of structure?
questions.note: A Brazil-nut tree produces a hard, woody fruit that holds numerous seeds arranged inside.

questions.question: Tahini is a paste made chiefly from which seeds?
questions.note: Tahini is made by grinding sesame seeds into a smooth paste.

questions.question: Which part of broccoli do people mainly eat?
questions.note: A broccoli head is a cluster of immature flower buds carried on branching stems.

questions.question: Why are some traditional pretzels dipped in lye before baking?
questions.note: The alkaline bath accelerates browning and creates the pretzel's distinctive crust and flavor.

questions.question: A cat uses its whiskers mainly as what kind of tool?
questions.note: Whiskers are specialized touch hairs that help cats sense nearby objects and air movement.

questions.question: A shark's skeleton is made mostly from what?
questions.note: Sharks and other elasmobranchs have skeletons made of cartilage rather than bone.

questions.question: What shape are a goat's pupils in ordinary light?
questions.note: Goats have horizontally elongated pupils that provide a broad view of their surroundings.

questions.question: How does a frog take in most of the water it needs?
questions.note: Frogs absorb water through a specialized patch of skin instead of drinking it normally.

questions.question: Where does a sea otter often store food while diving?
questions.note: Loose skin under each forearm forms a pocket where a sea otter can hold prey or a rock.

questions.question: Which bird can sustain backward flight?
questions.note: A hummingbird can reverse the angle of its wings to fly backward as well as hover.

questions.question: Ants exchange oxygen without having which organs?
questions.note: Ants have no lungs; air moves through tiny openings into a network of tracheal tubes.

questions.question: What type of blood vessel carries blood away from the heart?
questions.note: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, regardless of its oxygen content.

questions.question: Which clear part of the eye has no blood vessels and gets oxygen mainly from tears and air?
questions.note: The transparent cornea has no blood vessels; it receives oxygen from the air through the tear film.

questions.question: Which tree appears at the center of Lebanon's national flag?
questions.note: Lebanon's flag places a green cedar tree between two red horizontal bands.

questions.question: Which city sits on both the European and Asian sides of the Bosporus?
questions.note: The Bosporus divides Istanbul between a European shore and an Asian shore.

questions.question: Which national flag includes an open Bible in its coat of arms?
questions.note: The Dominican Republic's coat of arms, centered on its flag, includes an open Bible.

questions.question: Which present-day country contains the ancient city of Petra?
questions.note: The Nabataean rock-cut city of Petra lies in southern Jordan.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of the Inca road system?
questions.note: The Qhapaq Nan connected Inca territories for communication, trade, defense, and administration.

questions.question: Why does the Eiffel Tower become slightly taller in hot weather?
questions.note: Thermal expansion makes the iron structure grow by a few millimeters in summer heat.

questions.question: Which U.S. state is both the westernmost and easternmost by longitude?
questions.note: Alaska's Aleutian Islands cross the 180th meridian, placing the state in both east and west longitudes.

questions.question: The ancient city of Timbuktu is in which modern country?
questions.note: Timbuktu stands near the Niger River in the West African country of Mali.

questions.question: The Rosetta Stone repeats one decree in how many writing systems?
questions.note: The decree appears in hieroglyphic, Demotic, and ancient Greek scripts.

questions.question: In Monopoly, may a player collect rent while in Jail?
questions.note: The official rules allow a jailed player to buy and sell property, build, and collect rent.

questions.question: How many points is a blank tile worth in Scrabble?
questions.note: A blank may represent any letter but carries no point value.

questions.question: In standard chess, can a pawn promote to a second queen?
options: Only if the first queen was captured
questions.note: Promotion is not limited by pieces already on the board, so multiple queens are legal.

questions.question: Where are the original stuffed toys that inspired Winnie-the-Pooh displayed?
questions.note: Christopher Robin Milne's original Pooh, Tigger, Eeyore, Piglet, and Kanga toys are held by the New York Public Library.

questions.question: What was Mario called in his first appearance in Donkey Kong?
questions.note: The arcade character later known as Mario was originally identified as Jumpman.

questions.question: Every standard Tetris piece is built from how many equal squares?
questions.note: The name tetromino describes each shape made from four edge-connected squares.

questions.question: In UNO, when may you legally play a Wild Draw Four card?
options: Only when you have no card matching the current color
questions.note: The rules permit Wild Draw Four only when the player holds no card matching the current color.

questions.question: What object carries the inscription "One Ring to rule them all" in Tolkien's story?
questions.note: The fiery inscription appears on the One Ring when it is heated.

questions.question: In the original Pac-Man arcade game, what restores one of the ghosts to normal after it is eaten?
options: Its eyes returning to the ghost house
questions.note: An eaten ghost's eyes travel back to the central ghost house, where the ghost regenerates.

questions.question: What is the small sheath at the end of a shoelace called?
questions.note: An aglet is the sheath that binds a shoelace end and helps it pass through eyelets.

questions.question: QR codes were first developed to track parts in which industry?
questions.note: DENSO WAVE developed the QR Code in 1994 to improve component tracking in automobile manufacturing.

questions.question: In the original toilet-paper roll patent drawing, which way does the loose end hang?
questions.note: Seth Wheeler's 1891 patent drawing shows the perforated paper feeding over the top of the roll.

questions.question: Which came first: the metal food can or the can opener?
questions.note: Canned food appeared decades before dedicated openers; early cans were opened with tools such as hammers and chisels.

questions.question: What is the metal band that holds a pencil's eraser called?
questions.note: The crimped metal sleeve joining an eraser to a pencil is called a ferrule.

questions.question: In Grant Wood's American Gothic, what relationship did he imagine between the two figures?
questions.note: Wood described the stern pair as a farmer and his adult daughter, not a married couple.

questions.question: Rodin originally designed The Thinker as part of which larger work?
questions.note: The seated poet first appeared above the doorway in Rodin's monumental Gates of Hell.

questions.question: How many canvases make up Andy Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans?
questions.note: Warhol painted 32 separate canvases, one for each soup variety Campbell sold at the time.

questions.question: In Edvard Munch's account behind The Scream, where did the scream come from?
questions.note: Munch wrote that he sensed an infinite scream passing through nature while walking at sunset.

questions.question: What does the zipper-maker name YKK abbreviate?
questions.note: YKK comes from the former company name Yoshida Kogyo Kabushikikaisha.

decks.name: Set 4
decks.subtitle: Familiar subjects, surprising details, and rules worth remembering.

questions.question: Which film was the first animated feature nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture?
options: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
questions.note: Beauty and the Beast received a Best Picture nomination for the 1991 film year.

questions.question: What everyday object does Doctor Who's TARDIS resemble from the outside?
questions.note: Its faulty chameleon circuit leaves it disguised as a blue British police box.

questions.question: Which feature film is credited with popularizing synchronized spoken dialogue?
questions.note: The Jazz Singer, released in 1927, became the first feature-length motion picture with synchronized dialogue sequences.

questions.question: At which televised event did Michael Jackson first perform his famous moonwalk?
questions.note: Jackson unveiled the move during Billie Jean on the Motown 25 television special.

questions.question: Who supplied the distinctive speaking voice of E.T. in E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial?
questions.note: Pat Welsh provided E.T.'s principal speaking voice, with other sounds blended into the final track.

questions.question: What text is absent from the front cover of the Beatles album Abbey Road?
options: The album title and band name
questions.note: The iconic cover shows the four Beatles crossing Abbey Road without printing the band name or album title on the front.

questions.question: In The Matrix, which pill does Neo take to learn the truth?
questions.note: Neo chooses the red pill and wakes from the simulated world.

questions.question: Which television comedy follows the employees of the fictional Dunder Mifflin paper company?
questions.note: The US version of The Office centers on Dunder Mifflin's Scranton branch.

questions.question: In soccer, can a player be penalized for offside directly from a goal kick?
questions.note: The offside law specifically exempts players receiving the ball directly from a goal kick.

questions.question: In baseball, what happens when a batter bunts a foul ball with two strikes?
questions.note: Unlike an ordinary foul with two strikes, a foul bunt counts as strike three.

questions.question: How many points are needed to win the deciding fifth set in indoor volleyball, barring deuce?
questions.note: The deciding fifth set is played to 15 points, with a two-point winning margin.

questions.question: Which restriction applies when castling in chess?
options: The king may not cross an attacked square
The queen must still be on the board
The king must begin in check
questions.note: A king cannot castle out of, through, or into check.

questions.question: In Olympic freestyle swimming, which stroke must competitors use?
questions.note: Freestyle permits any stroke, though competitors almost always choose the fastest front crawl.

questions.question: How high is a tennis net at its center?
questions.note: The net is held down to 3 feet at the center, lower than its 3-foot-6-inch posts.

questions.question: How many goals by one player make a hat trick in ice hockey?
questions.note: A player records a hat trick by scoring three goals in one game.

questions.question: Must a baseball player who hits a home run still touch every base?
options: No, the ball is already dead
Only if a runner was on base
questions.note: The batter-runner must legally touch each base even after sending the ball out of play.

questions.question: A coffee "bean" is botanically what part of the coffee fruit?
questions.note: The so-called coffee bean is a seed found inside the coffee plant's fruit.

questions.question: Gelatin is produced by processing which animal protein?
questions.note: Gelatin forms when collagen from animal skin, bone, and connective tissue is processed and partially broken down.

questions.question: Traditional couscous granules are made chiefly from what?
questions.note: Couscous is traditionally made from moistened semolina rolled into tiny granules.

questions.question: Paprika is made by drying and grinding which plant part?
questions.note: Paprika is a powder made from dried fruits of Capsicum annuum peppers.

questions.question: Which part of the rhubarb plant is normally eaten?
questions.note: Rhubarb is grown for its thick edible leaf stalks; its leaf blades contain high levels of oxalic acid.

questions.question: Compared with white chicken eggs, brown chicken eggs are generally what?
questions.note: Shell color mostly reflects the hen's breed and does not make an egg more nutritious.

questions.question: What makes bread turn brown during toasting?
questions.note: Heat drives reactions between amino acids and sugars that create brown color and toasted flavors.

questions.question: What is the main ingredient in traditional Japanese miso?
questions.note: Miso is a fermented paste usually based on soybeans, salt, and koji.

questions.question: Which appeared on Earth first: sharks or trees?
questions.note: Shark ancestors predate the earliest known trees by tens of millions of years.

questions.question: Botanically, which fruit is a berry?
questions.note: Bananas develop from one ovary and meet the botanical definition of a berry.

questions.question: What is the largest living species of fish?
questions.note: The whale shark is the largest living fish species.

questions.question: What color is oxygen-poor human blood inside veins?
questions.note: Human blood remains red; veins look blue because skin and tissue alter reflected light.

questions.question: How many legs does an adult dragonfly have?
questions.note: Dragonflies are insects and have six legs, although they use them mainly for perching and catching prey.

questions.question: Sound usually travels faster through which medium?
options: It travels equally fast in all media
questions.note: Particles transmit vibrations more quickly in water than in air; sound cannot cross a vacuum.

questions.question: What is Earth's largest desert?
questions.note: Deserts are defined by low precipitation, making Antarctica the largest.

questions.question: Why does the Moon show nearly the same face to Earth?
options: Its rotation period matches its orbit
questions.note: The Moon rotates once in the same time it takes to orbit Earth, a state called synchronous rotation.

questions.question: The shortest recorded war, fought in 1896, involved Britain and which place?
questions.note: The Anglo-Zanzibar War ended after less than an hour of fighting.

questions.question: Why was Canberra selected as Australia's federal capital?
options: It was a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne
It had the only deep-water port
It was the first British settlement
questions.note: Canberra was chosen as a compromise location after rivalry between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.question: What do the Panama Canal's locks do to ships?
options: Tow them by cable across the ocean
Raise and lower them between water levels
questions.note: Lock chambers lift ships up to Gatun Lake and lower them again toward the opposite ocean.

questions.question: Which country has no permanent natural rivers?
questions.note: Saudi Arabia has seasonal wadis but no permanent rivers.

questions.question: Which statement about the Great Wall of China is accurate?
options: It is plainly visible from the Moon
It consists of many sections built over centuries
It was entirely built by one emperor
questions.note: Many dynasties built separate walls and fortifications; naked-eye visibility from the Moon is a myth.

questions.question: Which ancient ruler lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid?
questions.note: Cleopatra died in 30 BCE, over two millennia after the Great Pyramid was built.

questions.question: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
questions.note: Lesotho is an enclave whose entire boundary meets South Africa.

questions.question: Which sovereign state is the world's smallest by area?
questions.note: Vatican City occupies about 44 hectares and is the world's smallest independent state.

questions.question: What name does Mary Shelley give Frankenstein's creature in the novel?
questions.note: The novel never gives the creature a personal name; Frankenstein is his creator.

questions.question: What was Nintendo's original product when the company began in 1889?
questions.note: Nintendo began in Kyoto making handmade hanafuda playing cards.

questions.question: In Clue, which rooms are connected by secret passages?
questions.note: The four corner rooms form two secret-passage pairs that let a player cross the board.

questions.question: Which phrase does Sherlock Holmes never say exactly in Arthur Conan Doyle's original stories?
questions.note: Holmes says similar words separately, but the famous full phrase came from later adaptations.

questions.question: Which board game evolved from The Landlord's Game, designed to criticize monopolies?
questions.note: Elizabeth Magie patented The Landlord's Game decades before Monopoly became a commercial hit.

questions.question: What is the highest possible score for a single dart in standard darts?
questions.note: The treble 20 scores 60, which is higher than the 50-point inner bull.

questions.question: In Bram Stoker's Dracula, can Count Dracula move about during daylight?
options: Yes, but his powers are reduced
Only while disguised as a wolf
questions.note: Stoker's Dracula can appear by day, although daylight limits his supernatural abilities.

questions.question: In which work did Peter Pan first appear?
questions.note: J. M. Barrie introduced Peter Pan in the 1902 adult novel The Little White Bird.

questions.question: The first webcam was aimed at what object?
questions.note: Cambridge researchers pointed an early network camera at the Trojan Room coffee pot so colleagues could check whether coffee remained.

questions.question: Bluetooth wireless technology was named after which historical ruler?
questions.note: Bluetooth was named for Harald Bluetooth, a Danish king associated with uniting Denmark and Norway.

questions.question: What accidental observation helped Percy Spencer develop the microwave oven?
options: A candy bar melted in his pocket
Water froze beside a radar tube
questions.note: A candy bar melted while Spencer worked near an active magnetron, prompting experiments with food.

questions.question: What does the distress signal SOS officially stand for?
options: Nothing; it is not an abbreviation
questions.note: SOS was selected as a simple, distinctive Morse signal and was not created as an abbreviation.

questions.question: What does the name LEGO come from?
questions.note: Ole Kirk Kristiansen formed LEGO from the Danish phrase leg godt, meaning play well.

questions.question: Which came first?
options: They appeared in the same year
questions.note: Dobereiner's hydrogen lighter appeared in 1823, before John Walker's friction matches in 1826.

questions.question: A modern "tin can" is usually made mainly from what?
questions.note: Traditional food cans use steel sheet with a thin protective coating of tin.

questions.question: What does CAPTCHA stand for?
options: Computerized Access Test for Public Human Authentication
Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart
Central Authentication Protocol for Trusted Accounts
Computer Analysis Program That Checks Human Answers
questions.note: CAPTCHA expands to Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart.

questions.question: Which color was produced by the first widely used synthetic dye?
questions.note: William Perkin accidentally discovered the purple dye mauveine in 1856.

questions.question: What was the Louvre before it became a museum?
questions.note: The site began as a medieval fortress and later became a royal palace.

questions.question: Which common symbol was once called the octothorpe by telephone engineers?
questions.note: Bell Labs staff used octothorpe as a name for the # key on touch-tone telephones.

questions.question: The word "robot" entered popular use through a play written in which language?
questions.note: Karel Capek's Czech play R.U.R. popularized robot from a word related to forced labor.

questions.question: Which number does a standard roulette wheel contain that is neither red nor black?
questions.note: Zero is green; American wheels also include a green double zero.

questions.question: Why did ancient Greek and Roman statues often appear white to later viewers?
options: Their paint faded or wore away
questions.note: Many classical sculptures were brightly painted, but most surface pigment disappeared over time.

questions.question: What did the earliest known vending machine dispense?
questions.note: Hero of Alexandria described a coin-operated device that dispensed a measured amount of holy water.

questions.question: What is the dot above a lowercase i or j called?
questions.note: The small distinguishing mark above i and j is called a tittle.

questions.question: The cascading green code in The Matrix was adapted from recipes for what?
questions.note: Designer Simon Whiteley scanned characters from his wife's Japanese sushi cookbooks.

questions.question: In 2001: A Space Odyssey, what is the name of the spacecraft's computer?
questions.note: HAL 9000 controls the Discovery One and becomes the film's central antagonist.

questions.question: Which often-quoted line is never said exactly that way in Casablanca?
questions.note: Ilsa says "Play it, Sam," while Rick says "Play it"; nobody says "Play it again, Sam."

questions.question: What is the name of Ripley's orange cat in Alien?
questions.note: Jones, often called Jonesy, survives the Nostromo disaster with Ripley.

questions.question: Which animation method gives a-ha's "Take On Me" video its pencilled movement?
questions.note: Artists traced filmed live-action frames to create the video's shifting pencil-drawn world.

questions.question: What song wakes Phil each morning in Groundhog Day?
questions.note: The clock radio repeatedly plays Sonny and Cher's "I Got You Babe" at 6:00 a.m.

questions.question: The gangster movie watched by Kevin in Home Alone is what?
questions.note: Angels with Filthy Souls was a black-and-white scene created specially for Home Alone.

questions.question: Which Beatles album was recorded last, although it was not released last?
questions.note: Abbey Road was the final album the four Beatles recorded together; Let It Be reached shops later.

questions.question: Which Ghostbusters villain begins as a smiling advertising mascot?
questions.note: Ray accidentally chooses the familiar Stay Puft mascot as the form of the destructor.

questions.question: The famous tongue-and-lips logo was created for which rock band?
questions.note: John Pasche designed the tongue-and-lips emblem for the Rolling Stones in 1970.

questions.question: What is the minimum diameter of a regulation golf ball?
questions.note: The equipment rules require a golf ball to have a diameter of at least 1.680 inches.

questions.question: Why are NHL hockey pucks kept cold before games?
questions.note: Chilled rubber is less lively, so a cold puck bounces less than a warm one.

questions.question: In fencing, which weapon allows touches anywhere on the opponent's body?
questions.note: The epee target is the entire body; foil and sabre use restricted target areas.

questions.question: How high is the center of a regulation badminton net?
questions.note: Badminton laws set the net at 1.524 metres high in the center of the court.

questions.question: Which swimming stroke gives the individual medley its final leg?
questions.note: Individual medleys run butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke, then freestyle.

questions.question: In basketball, what is the restricted-area arc under the basket commonly called?
questions.note: A secondary defender inside the no-charge semicircle normally cannot draw a charging foul.

questions.question: In rugby union, how many points is a drop goal worth?
questions.note: A successful drop goal scores three points, the same as a penalty goal.

questions.question: Which chess piece starts each game beside a rook?
questions.note: The back rank begins rook, knight, bishop from each outer edge.

questions.question: From where must a legal shot put be released?
options: Close to the neck or chin
questions.note: The shot must begin close to the neck or chin and may not be dropped below that position during the putting action.

questions.question: Caesar salad was created in which country?
questions.note: Restaurateur Caesar Cardini devised the salad in Tijuana, Mexico, in the 1920s.

questions.question: German chocolate cake is named after what?
questions.note: Samuel German developed the sweet baking chocolate that gave the American cake its name.

questions.question: Traditional Japanese mochi is made chiefly from what?
questions.note: Mochi is prepared by steaming and pounding glutinous rice into an elastic paste.

questions.question: Maple syrup is concentrated from which fluid collected from maple trees?
questions.note: Producers tap maple trees for sap and boil away water to concentrate it into syrup.

questions.question: What makes a traditional pound cake a "pound" cake?
options: A pound of each main ingredient
questions.note: Early recipes used one pound each of flour, butter, sugar, and eggs.

questions.question: The fruit now called a kiwifruit was once widely marketed as what?
questions.note: New Zealand exporters replaced "Chinese gooseberry" with kiwifruit as overseas sales grew.

questions.question: Espresso is defined mainly by what?
questions.note: Espresso forces hot water under pressure through finely ground coffee; no special espresso bean is required.

questions.question: Cutting an onion releases an irritant that reaches which body part to trigger tears?
questions.note: Damaged onion cells release a volatile lachrymatory factor that reaches the eyes and stimulates tearing.

questions.question: What does crystallization usually mean for a jar of pure honey?
options: It has naturally formed glucose crystals
questions.note: Crystallization is a normal physical change and does not mean the honey has gone bad.

questions.question: How can a dolphin sleep without completely stopping its breathing?
options: One brain hemisphere rests at a time
questions.note: Dolphins use unihemispheric sleep, resting one side of the brain while the other remains alert enough to surface and breathe.

questions.question: What color is horseshoe-crab blood?
questions.note: Copper-containing hemocyanin makes horseshoe-crab blood blue.

questions.question: Why can astronauts become slightly taller while in orbit?
questions.note: With gravity no longer compressing the spine, the discs between vertebrae can expand.

questions.question: Which planet has an average density lower than liquid water?
questions.note: Saturn's average density is about 0.69 grams per cubic centimetre, less than water's.

questions.question: How many permanent teeth does a typical adult have, including wisdom teeth?
questions.note: A complete adult dentition contains 32 permanent teeth when all four wisdom teeth are present.

questions.question: Under ultraviolet light, platypus fur can glow which color?
questions.note: Researchers found that platypus fur absorbs ultraviolet light and fluoresces blue-green.

questions.question: What is the largest single bone in the human body?
questions.note: The thigh bone, or femur, is the body's longest and strongest single bone.

questions.question: What keeps Apollo astronauts' footprints on the Moon from quickly eroding?
options: Almost no wind or liquid water
questions.note: The Moon has no weather like Earth's, although micrometeorites will disturb the prints over very long periods.

questions.question: Which frog can survive with much of its body frozen during winter?
questions.note: Wood frogs survive winter by allowing ice to form in much of the body while glucose helps protect their cells.

questions.question: The town of Baarle is famous for a patchwork border between Belgium and which country?
questions.note: Belgian enclaves and Dutch counter-enclaves create an intricate border through Baarle.

questions.question: Which country's national anthem has no official lyrics?
questions.note: Spain's Marcha Real is one of the few national anthems without official words.

questions.question: Which city has hosted university teaching since before the Aztec Empire existed?
questions.note: Teaching existed at Oxford by 1096; the Aztec Empire formed in the 15th century.

questions.question: What is the southernmost national capital city?
questions.note: New Zealand's capital, Wellington, lies farther south than any other sovereign state capital.

questions.question: The Trans-Siberian Railway crosses how many time zones between Moscow and Vladivostok?
questions.note: The route stretches across eight time zones on its journey through Russia.

questions.question: Angel Falls, the world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, is in which country?
questions.note: Angel Falls drops from Auyan-tepui in southeastern Venezuela.

questions.question: Which country contains more ancient pyramids than Egypt?
questions.note: Sudan contains hundreds of Nubian pyramids, including major groups at Meroe.

questions.question: Mount Everest stands on the border between Nepal and which country?
questions.note: The summit of Everest lies on the Nepal-China border, with Tibet on the northern side.

questions.question: The word "salary" is historically linked to the Latin word for what?
questions.note: Salary comes through Latin salarium, a word derived from sal, meaning salt.

questions.question: What does the Monopoly mascot, Rich Uncle Pennybags, not wear?
questions.note: The mascot has a top hat and moustache but no monocle, despite a common false memory.

questions.question: What was Milton Bradley's 1860 precursor to The Game of Life called?
questions.note: Milton Bradley launched his company with The Checkered Game of Life in 1860.

questions.question: How many bonus points does a Scrabble player receive for using all seven rack tiles in one turn?
questions.note: Using all seven tiles in one play earns a 50-point bonus, commonly called a bingo.

questions.question: What is Oscar Wilde's only published novel?
questions.note: The Picture of Dorian Gray is Oscar Wilde's only novel.

questions.question: In the original British Cluedo, what is the murder victim called?
questions.note: The British game names the victim Dr Black; North American Clue renamed him Mr Boddy.

questions.question: Which number is opposite 20 on a standard dartboard?
questions.note: The standard board places 3 at the bottom, directly opposite 20 at the top.

questions.question: In The Hobbit, what kind of mark does Gandalf put on Bilbo's door?
questions.note: Gandalf scratches a secret sign on the green door so the dwarves can identify the burglar's home.

questions.question: Which Alice in Wonderland character is a caricature of author Lewis Carroll?
questions.note: The stammering Dodo is widely understood as Carroll's self-caricature: Do-Do-Dodgson.

questions.question: In a standard deck of cards, which king is traditionally shown without a moustache?
questions.note: In the familiar Anglo-American design, the king of hearts is the lone clean-shaven king.

questions.question: What does the raised red flag on a rural U.S. mailbox signal?
questions.note: A raised carrier-signal flag tells the postal carrier that outgoing mail is waiting in the box.

questions.question: What is the wavy inner layer of corrugated cardboard called?
questions.note: The arched paper between the flat linerboards is called fluting; its shape gives corrugated board rigidity.

questions.question: The side brushes along many escalators are intended mainly to do what?
options: Keep feet and clothing away from the edge
questions.note: Skirt brushes provide a tactile warning that encourages riders to keep away from the gap beside the moving steps.

questions.question: What do the black dots around a car windscreen mainly help do?
questions.note: The ceramic frit shades the urethane sealant from ultraviolet light and creates a gradual visual edge.

questions.question: Why do ISO A-series paper sizes keep the same proportions when cut in half?
options: Their sides use a square-root-of-two ratio
Their area is always one square metre
questions.note: The 1-to-square-root-of-two aspect ratio reproduces itself when the sheet is halved across its longer side.

questions.question: Why did paint in collapsible metal tubes matter to 19th-century painters?
options: It removed the need for brushes
questions.note: Portable, resealable tubes let artists carry fresh paint outdoors without preparing pigments on site.

questions.question: Who posed for the farmer and daughter in Grant Wood's American Gothic?
questions.note: Wood used his dentist, Byron McKeeby, and his sister, Nan Wood Graham, as separate models.

questions.question: Hokusai's The Great Wave was made using which printmaking method?
questions.note: The Great Wave is a color woodblock print from Hokusai's series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.

questions.question: In Magritte's The Treachery of Images, what appears below the painted pipe?
options: Words saying it is not a pipe
questions.note: The French sentence "Ceci n'est pas une pipe" reminds viewers that the painting is an image, not a pipe.

decks.name: Set 6
decks.subtitle: A tougher final-deck mix of familiar facts and sharp details.

questions.question: In Jaws, what kind of shark is hunted off Amity Island?
questions.note: The film calls the attacking animal a great white shark.

questions.question: Which Fleetwood Mac album includes "Dreams" and "Go Your Own Way"?
questions.note: Both songs appeared on the band's 1977 album Rumours.

questions.question: What is the name of the newspaper where Clark Kent works?
questions.note: Clark Kent works as a reporter for Metropolis's Daily Planet.

questions.question: Which composer wrote the scores for Jaws, E.T., and Jurassic Park?
questions.note: John Williams composed the music for all three Steven Spielberg films.

questions.question: Which singer released the 1985 album Hounds of Love?
questions.note: Kate Bush wrote and produced Hounds of Love, which includes "Running Up That Hill."

questions.question: In Citizen Kane, what object bears the name "Rosebud"?
questions.note: Rosebud is the name painted on Kane's childhood sled.

questions.question: Which actor directed and starred in Unforgiven?
questions.note: Clint Eastwood directed the 1992 western and played William Munny.

questions.question: What was Freddie Mercury's birth name?
questions.note: Freddie Mercury was born Farrokh Bulsara in Zanzibar.

questions.question: Which TV detective is known for saying "Just one more thing"?
questions.note: Lieutenant Columbo often returns with the disarming phrase "Just one more thing."

questions.question: In baseball, how many strikes normally retire a batter?
questions.note: A third strike completes a strikeout, subject to the uncaught-third-strike rule.

questions.question: How long is a standard Olympic swimming pool?
questions.note: World Aquatics specifies a 50-metre pool for long-course competition.

questions.question: How many stumps make up a cricket wicket?
questions.note: A wicket consists of three wooden stumps topped by two bails.

questions.question: Which chess piece must stay on squares of one color?
questions.note: A bishop moves diagonally, so it can never leave its starting square color.

questions.question: In Formula One, what flag orders a driver to stop because they are disqualified?
questions.note: A black flag shown with a car number tells that driver to return to the pits.

questions.question: What is the maximum break in snooker without a free ball?
questions.note: Fifteen reds with blacks, followed by all six colors, totals 147.

questions.question: In basketball, how long may an NBA player remain in the opponents' lane on offense?
questions.note: The offensive three-second rule limits a player in the lane while their team controls the ball.

questions.question: Which athletics event uses a 7.26-kilogram metal ball in the men's competition?
questions.note: The senior men's shot weighs 7.26 kilograms, or 16 pounds.

questions.question: Which French sauce is made by emulsifying egg yolks and butter?
questions.note: Hollandaise is a warm emulsion of egg yolks, butter, and an acid such as lemon juice.

questions.question: What grain is traditionally used to make Japanese sake?
questions.note: Sake is brewed from polished rice with water, yeast, and koji mold.

questions.question: Which cheese is traditionally used in a Greek salad?
questions.note: The traditional horiatiki salad is topped with feta cheese.

questions.question: What gives Earl Grey tea its characteristic flavor?
questions.note: Oil from bergamot citrus peel supplies Earl Grey's distinctive aroma.

questions.question: Which nut forms the base of traditional marzipan?
questions.note: Marzipan is a paste made chiefly from ground almonds and sugar.

questions.question: What type of pastry is used for profiteroles?
questions.note: Profiterole shells are baked from choux pastry, which puffs from steam.

questions.question: Which country is the origin of the cheese Gouda?
questions.note: Gouda is named for the Dutch city where the cheese was historically traded.

questions.question: In cooking, what does it mean to julienne a vegetable?
questions.note: A julienne cut produces thin, matchstick-shaped strips.

questions.question: Which blood cells carry most of the oxygen in the human body?
questions.note: Hemoglobin inside red blood cells binds and transports oxygen.

questions.question: What is the largest species of living penguin?
questions.note: The emperor penguin is the tallest and heaviest living penguin species.

questions.question: Which element has the chemical symbol W?
questions.note: Tungsten uses W from its older name, wolfram.

questions.question: What is the only mammal capable of sustained true flight?
questions.note: Bats generate powered flight; other so-called flying mammals only glide.

questions.question: Which layer of Earth is liquid?
questions.note: Earth's outer core is liquid iron and nickel around a solid inner core.

questions.question: A narwhal's tusk is actually an enlarged what?
questions.note: The spiral tusk is an elongated canine tooth, usually on the left side.

questions.question: Which planet has the shortest day in the Solar System?
questions.note: Jupiter rotates in about 10 hours, faster than any other planet.

questions.question: What is measured on the Mohs scale?
questions.note: The Mohs scale ranks minerals by their resistance to scratching.

questions.question: Which organ produces insulin in the human body?
questions.note: Beta cells in the pancreas produce the hormone insulin.

questions.question: What kind of animal is an axolotl?
questions.note: The axolotl is a salamander that normally retains aquatic larval traits as an adult.

questions.question: Which modern city was once called Constantinople?
questions.note: Constantinople became the official name Istanbul in Turkey in 1930.

questions.question: Machu Picchu was built by which civilization?
questions.note: The Inca built Machu Picchu in the Andes during the 15th century.

questions.question: Which treaty formally ended World War I between Germany and the Allies?
questions.note: Germany and the Allies signed the Treaty of Versailles in 1919.

questions.question: Which African country was formerly known as Abyssinia?
questions.note: Abyssinia was a historical European name for Ethiopia.

questions.question: Which country almost completely surrounds The Gambia?
questions.note: Senegal surrounds The Gambia on three sides; the country's western edge meets the Atlantic.

questions.question: Which narrow sea lies entirely within Turkey and connects the Black Sea route to the Aegean?
questions.note: The Sea of Marmara connects through the Bosporus to the Black Sea and through the Dardanelles to the Aegean.

questions.question: Which empire used quipu, systems of knotted cords, for record keeping?
questions.note: Inca administrators encoded numerical records on knotted quipu cords.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.note: Amelia Earhart completed the first female solo Atlantic crossing in 1932.

questions.question: Which national capital is widely recognized as the world's coldest?
questions.note: Mongolia's Ulaanbaatar has an extremely cold continental climate and is commonly identified as the coldest national capital.

questions.question: Which material helped ancient Roman marine concrete harden under water?
questions.note: Roman builders mixed lime with volcanic ash, producing hydraulic concrete that could set under water.

questions.question: Who wrote The Name of the Rose?
questions.note: Italian scholar and novelist Umberto Eco published The Name of the Rose in 1980.

questions.question: In Scrabble, how many points is the letter Q worth in English-language play?
questions.note: Q and Z are the two 10-point tiles in English Scrabble.

questions.question: Which Shakespeare play contains Rosencrantz and Guildenstern?
questions.note: Rosencrantz and Guildenstern are Hamlet's former school friends.

questions.question: Which novel opens with the line "Call me Ishmael"?
options: The Old Man and the Sea
questions.note: Ishmael introduces himself in the first sentence of Herman Melville's Moby-Dick.

questions.question: In standard Monopoly, which property comes immediately after Go?
questions.note: Mediterranean Avenue is the first purchasable property after Go.

questions.question: Who created the detective Hercule Poirot?
questions.note: Agatha Christie introduced Belgian detective Hercule Poirot in The Mysterious Affair at Styles.

questions.question: Which fantasy novel centers on the hobbit Bilbo Baggins?
questions.note: Bilbo is the reluctant burglar and central character of J.R.R. Tolkien's The Hobbit.

questions.question: When may a pawn capture en passant in chess?
options: Only on the immediately following move
questions.note: An en passant capture is legal only on the move immediately after the opposing pawn advances two squares.

questions.question: What board game was originally called Lexiko?
questions.note: Alfred Mosher Butts developed Lexiko, which evolved into Scrabble.

questions.question: Who patented the first practical telephone in the United States?
questions.note: Alexander Graham Bell received U.S. Patent No. 174,465 for the telephone in 1876.

questions.question: Which artist painted The Persistence of Memory?
questions.note: Salvador Dali painted the famous melting clocks in 1931.

questions.question: What did Johannes Gutenberg's European press use to reproduce text?
questions.note: Gutenberg combined movable metal type with a mechanical press in 15th-century Europe.

questions.question: Which architect designed the large glass pyramid at the Louvre?
questions.note: I. M. Pei designed the glass pyramid that opened at the Louvre in 1989.

questions.question: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
questions.note: Michelangelo painted the chapel ceiling between 1508 and 1512.

questions.question: What phrase did Thomas Edison recite in his early demonstration of recorded sound?
options: To be or not to be
questions.note: Edison recited "Mary had a little lamb" into his tinfoil phonograph during an early demonstration.

questions.question: Which photographic process gave blueprints their characteristic blue color?
questions.note: The cyanotype process uses iron compounds to produce a stable Prussian-blue image and became the basis of blueprint copying.

questions.question: Which photography company introduced the Brownie camera in 1900?
questions.note: Eastman Kodak sold the simple Brownie camera for one dollar at launch.

questions.question: What are the individual small pieces in a mosaic called?
questions.note: Mosaics form images from small pieces of stone, glass, or other material called tesserae.

questions.question: What was the first synthetic plastic called?
questions.note: Leo Baekeland patented Bakelite, the first fully synthetic plastic, in 1909.
